note: Score cue for the soundtrack. Committed so a regeneration is reproducible rather than a fishing trip: model, prompt, seed, steps and sampler are the artifact, not just the idea. Rendered by scripts/render-score.mjs, baked by scripts/bake-audio.mjs; raw renders stay gitignored under assets/audio-src/raw/.

musical.why: Owner's direction: sparse, emotional, moving lo-fi instrumental -- not crowded, minimal effects. 74 bpm is lo-fi tempo: unhurried enough that the quiet scenes breathe, steady enough to anchor a scroll. On SA3 both bpm and key are PROSE, so they are requests rather than conditioning inputs -- which costs nothing here, because nothing has to phase-lock against anything any more.
musical.attack: The percussion must carry ATTACK even though the genre is soft. The scroll has no other rhythmic anchor, and fx.audioPulse drives the halftone breathe off the music bus, so a cue with smeared transients gives the visual nothing to move on either. Lo-fi is band-limited and warm AROUND its transients, not mushy through them.
musical.consequence: The quiet valleys (cover, origin, terminal are intensity 1) were designed around a restrained bed. arrangement() in lib/audio/score.ts holds the single cue down and under a lowpass there, so the mix darkens and recedes instead of merely turning down. Worth an ear on the cover and the terminal specifically.

cues.prompt: Sparse lo-fi instrumental trio in B flat major with a close-miked felt piano lead, warm upright double bass, and a brushed drum kit, supported by faint dry room tone and audible fingertip noise on the bass strings, with crisp rim clicks and a brushed snare with a sharp leading edge, leaving long silences between phrases for a melancholy but hopeful patient build, dry room, minimal processing, clean defined high end, no vocals, no synth pads, no strings, no guitar. BPM: 74. Length: 120 seconds
cues.promptNotes: Prose, not tags: SA3 is conditioned by t5gemma on one flowing sentence, and the shipped ComfyUI template's own reprompter targets exactly this shape -- style, lead instruments, supporting layers, percussion, mood, BPM, length. The DELETIONS still matter as much as the additions: no 'tape saturation' and no 'warm analog pads', because both are literal instructions to remove high frequencies and supply attackless texture. Every surviving descriptor either names an instrument or names an attack.
cues.intent: The single master cue, shipped whole. NOT split into stems -- owner's call, and it is the honest one too: a Demucs split of a three-piece trio bleeds piano into the drums stem and cymbals into the bass stem, and the runtime was paying three times the decoded memory for that.

samplerNotes: The distilled checkpoint fixes the sampler settings rather than offering them: 8 steps, cfg 1, lcm/simple, straight off the shipped ComfyUI template (audio_stable_audio_3_medium.json). cfg 1 means the negative branch is never evaluated, so a negative prompt would be inert -- steering lives entirely in the positive prose. The non-distilled sibling (stable_audio_3_medium_base.safetensors) is also on disk and does take cfg; it is not what this cue is rendered with.
mixLaw: Wall-clock locked, gain-mixed by t. NOT scrubbed: real music has rhythmic identity and scrubbing it by scroll position sounds like a turntable. The cue loops on its own clock; only its GAIN and lowpass cutoff are a pure function of t and velocity, which stays scrub-safe by construction.
